Liam: Seaview Ops reported a discrepancy on INV-2026-1203. Looks like both a downgrade proration and a promo proration applied; net credit is larger than expected. Can we correct? @Noor
Noor: Can you paste the invoice rows? will need numbers to approve reversal.
Liam: Yep, snippet below:
```
Invoice: INV-2026-1203
Line 1: Monthly subscription - Seaview Pro - $12,000
Line 2: Downgrade prorate refund -$4,000
Line 3: Promo PRORATE-DEC refund -$4,000
Total after credits: $4,000 (expected $8,000 -> one of the prorates shouldn't have applied)
```
billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-1203 posted 2026-12-03T16:45:12Z. Prorate and promo refunds both applied. Source tags: subscription-change, promo-engine.
SeaviewOps: Seaview confirms they only asked for the subscription downgrade prorate; promo shouldn't apply because promo TTL expired on 2026-11-30. They want the extra $4,000 reversed and a CN for their records.
Noor: Sounds like the promo engine didn't check promo end_date when recalculating after the downgrade. Two options: (A) issue refund reversal $4,000 to card, (B) apply reversing credit note CN-2026-1281 as account debit. Seaview preference?
SeaviewOps: Please refund to card and include a short explanation we can share with our accounting team.
CFO-Jane: Approve refund $4,000 and CN-2026-1281 "reversal - erroneous promo proration". Noor, please route to Payments and include apology. Also tag eng for a fix: FIN-9270 to add promo expiry guard to recompute path.
Noor: On it. Creating reversal CN-2026-1281 and opening FIN-9270 for eng. Routing refund to Payments now.
billing-bot: Refund request CN-2026-1281 created and queued. Estimated processing: 48 hours. Ticket FIN-9270 filed and assigned to eng-runtime.
Liam: Refund processed and CN emailed to Seaview. FIN-9270 remains open until eng confirms the codeguard. Closing loop once eng confirms. :white_check_mark:
